extracted.intended_audience: undergraduate students in a transition/introductory proofs course (and instructors adopting the textbook)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for students learning to construct, write, read, and communicate mathematical proofs in a first college-level proof course (transition course). Emphasizes standard proof methods, logical thinking, and mathematical communication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop logical thinking skills
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text lists developing logical thinking as a primary goal of the course/text; implies exercises and instruction aimed at improving students' ability to reason correctly and follow/construct logical arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop abstract thinking in a proof-oriented setting
rubrics_metrics.description: develop the ability to think more abstractly in a proof-oriented setting;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students should progress from concrete examples to abstract formulations and be able to manipulate and reason about abstract mathematical objects as required in proofs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construct and write mathematical proofs using standard methods
rubrics_metrics.description: develop the ability to construct and write mathematical proofs using standard methods of mathematical proof including direct proofs, proof by contradiction, mathematical induction, case analysis, and counterexamples;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect competence in a range of proof techniques: direct proof, proof by contradiction, mathematical induction, case analysis, and constructing counterexamples; emphasis on both construction (strategy) and clear written presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read and understand written mathematical proofs
rubrics_metrics.description: develop the ability to read and understand written mathematical proofs;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students should be able to parse, follow, and critically evaluate others' proofs, not just produce their own; comprehension skills are an explicit learning objective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop creative thinking and problem solving talents
rubrics_metrics.description: develop talents for creative thinking and problem solving;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond formal techniques, the course aims to foster creativity in approaching unfamiliar problems and devising proof strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improve quality of communication in mathematics
rubrics_metrics.description: improve their quality of communication in mathematics, which includes improving writing techniques, reading comprehension, and oral communication in mathematics;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communication quality covers mathematical writing (clarity, structure, notation), reading comprehension of mathematical texts, and oral presentation of mathematical arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand the nature of mathematics and its language
rubrics_metrics.description: better understand the nature of mathematics and its language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students should gain metacognitive understanding of what mathematics is, how mathematical language functions, and how proofs convey mathematical truth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis on writing in mathematics
rubrics_metrics.description: Important feature: Emphasis on writing in mathematics;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The book foregrounds written exposition—students are expected to practice and be evaluated on clear, well-structured mathematical writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instruction in the process of constructing proofs
rubrics_metrics.description: Important feature: instruction in the process of constructing proofs;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pedagogy focuses on the step-by-step process of discovering, planning, and assembling proofs (not only on final polished proofs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis on active learning
rubrics_metrics.description: Important feature: an emphasis on active learning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Course materials and activities are designed for student engagement (e.g., beginning activities, exercises, progress checks) rather than purely passive reading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete beginning activities before working sections
rubrics_metrics.description: Preview activities in Version 2.1 were renamed to beginning activities in Version 3 to emphasize that these activities are meant to be completed before starting the rest of the section and are not just a short preview of what is to come in the rest of the section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pedagogical requirement: students should do these beginning activities as preparatory work prior to engaging with the rest of each section; they are substantive and foundational rather than optional previews.
